note: What each guard CANNOT catch. Every bug on 2026-08-23 was a check that was right in principle and asked a question whose answer could not reveal the fault — not a broken guard, a guard aimed slightly beside the thing it guards. We declare blind spots for every agent and declared none for guards, so a guard asking the wrong question looked identical to one that works.
law: Writing the sentence IS the work. Anybody made to write 'measures elapsed time, not whether a scheduled run happened' would have seen the gap before it cost a morning. A blind spot too vague to reveal a gap is not a blind spot.

schema-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: Values. A file with every key present and an index of 8,123,456 passes every structural test ever written — shape checking cannot see whether a number is absurd.

flag-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: A gate that is registered, owned, documented and simply wrong. It verifies each flag exists once with an owner and a trigger; it has no view on whether the trigger is the right trigger.

memory-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether a law is CORRECT. It checks the knowledge base is current, readable and cross-referenced. A wrong law, perfectly formatted and reachable from the entry point, passes cleanly.
memory-guard.mjs.coveredBy: the falsifier, and being wrong in public

competence-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether a declared principle is TRUE. It enforces that every specialist declares sourced principles, failure modes, blind spots and a recheck date. A confidently wrong principle with a real citation passes.
competence-guard.mjs.coveredBy: the teacher, and the recheck date

knowledge-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether a source is any good. It requires every fact to carry sources, a date and a falsifier. Three secondary sources agreeing with each other satisfied it — and our own catalogue disproved the number.
knowledge-guard.mjs.coveredBy: verify-work's secondary-consensus check, added after exactly that

content-sanity.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether prose is GOOD. It catches labels in prose slots, unresolved templates, truncation and copy too short to be an explanation. A fluent, well-formed, entirely wrong sentence passes.

layout-check.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether a design looks GOOD. It measures clipping, overlap and empty panels against real font metrics. Geometry is not taste and a balanced, ugly page passes.

card-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the IMAGE is right. It reads the SVG source, so a card back served as a 200 PNG at correct dimensions passed everything — the bytes were valid and the picture was of the wrong thing.
card-guard.mjs.coveredBy: reading image URLs from source data rather than constructing them, and eyes

slop-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: A grouping that IS in the data and still means nothing. It enforces that every grouping derives from a held field or an openly stored list; a technically-derived and utterly boring grouping passes.

verify-work.mjs.cannotCatch: Reasoning. It checks whether output carries what a defensible claim must carry. The pooled-cohort error that nearly retired a correct thesis would have passed it cleanly.
verify-work.mjs.coveredBy: the decision log, which grades predictions rather than logic

bias-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: Its own bias. It was written by the same party it audits, and its measure of whether the machines are calibrated is a count the machines produce.
bias-guard.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler catching what the machines miss — the ratio IS the score

publish-assert.mjs.cannotCatch: Anything published through a path it does not read. Hand-minted cards went straight to Tyler twice, once with a wrong price and once meaningless, and this never saw either.
publish-assert.mjs.coveredBy: verify-work's ungated-publication check, added after exactly that

windowless-price-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: A figure with a window that is WRONG. It requires a date range; it cannot tell whether the range is accurate or whether the provider is describing it honestly.
windowless-price-guard.mjs.coveredBy: the graded-window probe, which measures rather than asks

domain-plausibility.mjs.cannotCatch: An implausible value that is nevertheless true. Its rules encode what we believe about the hobby, so a genuine market shock reads as a filter fault — it names our own filter as first suspect, which is right almost always and wrong sometimes.

guard-audit.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether a wired guard asks the right question. It verifies guards exist, are connected and run in order. The heartbeat was wired, ordered, running — and green through a failed run.

heartbeat.mjs.cannotCatch: A run that fires, succeeds, and produces wrong data. It now detects missed scheduled runs; it has no view on whether a completed run did anything useful.
knownPatterns: elapsed time as a proxy for an event
heartbeat.mjs.history: Allowed 30 hours so a LATE run would not cry wolf, which is exactly the window a SKIPPED run hides in. Reported green through a failed fetch on 2026-08-23.

qa-gate.mjs.cannotCatch: A number that is fresh, thick and wrong. It checks sample size, staleness and coverage — 26 listings kept from 150 fetched cleared every threshold while our own filter had eaten the market.

voice-lint.mjs.cannotCatch: Copy that is on-voice and says nothing. It catches hype, hedging and forbidden phrasing. The word 'chase' published as an entire explanation passed it — perfectly on-voice, perfectly meaningless.

jargon-lint.mjs.cannotCatch: A term we have taught badly. It flags unexplained jargon; it cannot tell whether the explanation given is any good, and 'the 9 rarely pays — only the 10' had a tooltip nobody could parse.

falsifier.mjs.cannotCatch: A thesis it is testing WRONGLY. It reported RT-5 TRIPPED because it pooled two cohorts the thesis explicitly contrasts — the thesis was 11 of 12 accurate and the test was measuring the average of a contrast. It matches card names when splitting RT-5 cohorts, which is the substring shape — mitigated by word boundaries and a hand-checked twelve-card set, and worth revisiting the moment that set grows.
falsifier.mjs.coveredBy: the contrastive-thesis guard in negative-tests, added after exactly that

correction-hunter.mjs.cannotCatch: A figure that never moves. It re-checks published numbers that changed; a price frozen for a month is a claim too, and it is invisible here.
correction-hunter.mjs.coveredBy: the teacher raised exactly this question

rasterize-cards.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the rendered image is CORRECT. It confirms a PNG was produced at the right size. A card back renders identically to a card front.
rasterize-cards.mjs.coveredBy: reading image URLs from source, and eyes

build-corrections.mjs.cannotCatch: NOT A GUARD. It generates the public corrections page. Listed in the audit because the audit tracks pipeline steps as well as checks, and conflating the two is how a generator gets read as a safety net. It also writes font stacks in the shorthand form, which is the shape that let four pages render headings in Times — acknowledged and fixed, kept on the record because the shape recurs.

pre-mortem.mjs.cannotCatch: A shape it has never been bitten by. Every pattern here was added AFTER something shipped, so the table is a record of our history, not a model of risk — it is structurally blind to the next novel failure and will stay so until that one costs a morning too. It also matches on SOURCE TEXT, so a guard that carries a shape inside a string or a comment reads as carrying the shape, and one that expresses the same fault through a helper or a computed value reads as clean.
pre-mortem.mjs.coveredBy: Nothing automatic. New shapes arrive only from a real failure being written up — which is why the report matters more than the scan.

editor-smoke.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the page LOOKS right, and whether the images actually resolve. It runs the emitted script against a minimal DOM and confirms cards and themes render — it has no browser, no layout, no network, so a page that loads perfectly and shows 24 card backs passes cleanly.
editor-smoke.mjs.coveredBy: CC with screenshots, and the constructed-URL fallback
editor-smoke.mjs.history: Written after the editor shipped three times in two days rendering nothing — verified to PARSE each time, never verified to WORK.

tease-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: A tease that withholds perfectly and is boring. It checks that nothing names the product; it has no view on whether the mystery is INTERESTING, and 'it arrives in a box' withholds everything and might intrigue nobody.
tease-guard.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler, and whether anybody replies asking what it is
tease-guard.mjs.history: Written after 'Catch'em Guards ???' shipped — the name answered the question the tag was pretending to withhold, and 'not a toploader, not a binder' then named the category while sounding like a denial. Nobody was checking.

creators-smoke.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the pairings are any GOOD. It confirms the page loads, renders pairings and images, and that every inline handler is reachable. It has no view on whether a pairing is worth posting.
creators-smoke.mjs.history: Written after every button on the portal was found dead — grab, setup, pick and toX all declared, none on window, and a top-level await inside a non-async grab() meant the whole script never ran. It parsed perfectly the entire time.

live-smoke.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the slides are worth talking about. It proves the two views stay synced, that the presenter always sees a confidence tier, and that no unverified claim reaches the overlay as stated fact. It has no view on whether a prompt would actually start a good segment.
live-smoke.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler using it live, and the post-outcome log
live-smoke.mjs.history: Found two real bugs on its first run: BroadcastChannel does not replay, so the audience opened blank whenever it started after the presenter, which is the normal order; and the audience posted its hello BEFORE assigning onmessage, so it could not hear the answer.

offline-smoke.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the images actually RESOLVE. It proves the page renders its catalogue with no network at all and that the srcs are well-formed. A page rendering 36 broken-image icons would pass.
offline-smoke.mjs.coveredBy: CC with a real browser, and Tyler opening it
offline-smoke.mjs.history: Written after I certified the editor as working using a harness that supplied a FAKE FETCH which always succeeded. Opened from file://, Chrome blocks fetch of a sibling file, INDEX stayed empty, and no images, no themes and no search results all followed from that single cause.

theme-smoke.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether a theme's output is INTERESTING. It proves every theme produces something at its own declared counts and that no two return identical card sets. A theme producing six dull pairings passes cleanly.
theme-smoke.mjs.coveredBy: the post-outcome log, and Tyler clicking through
theme-smoke.mjs.history: Written after Tyler found that only the artist themes worked, two returned identical results, and the rest produced nothing. Cause: buildIdeas switched on theme ID, so a theme without a branch failed silently, and artist-career and first-and-last shared one. It then found three more faults immediately, including a bestAt of 'late evening' where card counts belonged, and two themes that were the same theme written twice.

editor-hostile.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the abuse it survives is the abuse a real person commits. It tries what I could think of, which is not the same as what somebody will do.
editor-hostile.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler using it, and CC with a browser

editor-copy-rules.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the copy is GOOD. It proves nothing asserts, names a grade or leaks a JS value. A dull line that breaks no rule passes.
editor-copy-rules.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler using it, and CC with a browser

editor-claim-match.mjs.cannotCatch: A claim that is wrong about something OUTSIDE the cards. It checks counts, duplicates, named artists and card existence — not whether the underlying fact is true.
editor-claim-match.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler using it, and CC with a browser

editor-money-credit.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the prices are ACCURATE. It checks for absurd values and for the unpriced count being shown, not for a price being right.
editor-money-credit.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler using it, and CC with a browser

rating-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the derivation is a GOOD one. It proves every rating names a printed field and that refused ratings stay refused. It has no view on whether 'an unevolved Basic at 60 HP' is actually a fair proxy for cute — that is a judgement, and only Tyler and the outcome log can settle it.
rating-guard.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler, and whether the filters find what people expect
rating-guard.mjs.history: Written alongside the bios. Tyler asked for cuteness, comedy and popularity ratings; the honest version derives each from a printed field and the dishonest version is me assigning scores that feel right. Popularity and likeness were REFUSED outright for having no signal, and this guard exists so they cannot quietly reappear.

crop-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: Where X ACTUALLY crops. 1.25 is our best understanding of the timeline crop and it is not documented by X — if the real number is lower, every layout passes this guard and still clips. The margin is protection against rounding, not against a wrong constant.
crop-guard.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler, who is the only person who can see a real timeline
crop-guard.mjs.history: Written after the 2x2 clipped at the top. I had targeted EXACTLY 1.25 — the crop line itself — so there was zero tolerance for rounding or device pixel ratio. Designing to a limit means failing at the limit.

ask-smoke.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the cards it returns are the RIGHT ones. It proves every prompt fills the tray; it has no view on whether "something dark" returned anything actually dark.
ask-smoke.mjs.history: Written after seven of eleven prompts left the tray empty. The box promised a post and handed back a filtered grid, and the cause was thirteen word-boundary escapes emitting as BACKSPACE characters so every match silently failed.

evo-smoke.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the CARD chosen at each stage is the nicest one available. It proves the line is the right line and the right length; it has no view on whether a nicer Charmeleon existed.
evo-smoke.mjs.history: Written after "charizard evolution from 151" announced Charizard and returned Chansey and Blissey. Sixteen named lines are now checked on every build.

journey-smoke.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the finished image LOOKS right. It proves a typed sentence reaches a drawn image, with images working and with every image failing. It has no view on whether the composition is any good.
journey-smoke.mjs.history: Written after Tyler used the Charizard prompt and it failed on a build I had just audited as green. Five earlier tests all stopped at the tray and none pressed Make the image, and every one made images succeed — so the compose throwing on the first card that would not load was invisible.

audit-honesty.mjs.cannotCatch: A guard that tests the failing case BADLY. It checks that a failing path is exercised at all, not that the assertion afterwards is meaningful.
audit-honesty.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler, who keeps finding what the audits miss
audit-honesty.mjs.history: Written after three audits reported green and were wrong, each with the same shape: a test that FAKED the thing that actually breaks. Its first run flagged twelve guards, most of them false positives, and had to be narrowed to what each guard EXERCISES — a check that cries wolf gets muted, which is the lesson I logged that morning and then ignored writing this.

fuzz.mjs.cannotCatch: A bug that needs a SPECIFIC realistic sequence rather than a random one. It generates from real vocabulary plus noise, so it explores widely and shallowly — it will not find something that takes six deliberate steps in one exact order.
fuzz.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler, who has found six things no test imagined
fuzz.mjs.history: Written because every other test checks something I already imagined — ten prompts I chose, fourteen abuses I thought of. Its FIRST RUN found three crashes: startStreak with an unknown filter, and todaysCard or confirmPosted with no streak, all reading .test on undefined. Then it immediately caught my own fix using the wrong parameter name.

surface-parity.mjs.cannotCatch: A mobile lesson we have not learned yet. It encodes four rules from four real failures; it knows nothing about the fifth.
surface-parity.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler, on whichever surface he opens next
surface-parity.mjs.history: Written after the composite page failed on mobile with the EXACT combination I had already fixed in the editor — hires for display, eager loading, no fallback. The real bug was not the image size, it was that I fixed the file Tyler happened to be holding three separate times and never carried one fix across. Its first run found three MORE surfaces with the same problem.

device-gauntlet.mjs.cannotCatch: Real rendering. It proves the script parses, boots and produces cards in six hostile profiles — it has no view on whether anything LOOKS right, whether images actually load from a real CDN, or whether a real Safari has a quirk none of these profiles model.
device-gauntlet.mjs.history: Written after three wrong guesses at a mobile 'script error'. It reproduced the failure on the FIRST run: one top-level throw stops initialization halfway, every let below stays uninitialized, the boot timer fires into a dead binding, and the page is blank.

prompt-correctness.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the right cards are the BEST cards. It proves a Charizard prompt returns Charizards and a Fire prompt returns Fire — it has no view on whether those particular Charizards are the ones worth posting.
prompt-correctness.mjs.history: Written after Tyler said the prompts were still returning wrong cards for the third time. ask-smoke had been green throughout because it only checked cards APPEARED — a gap I documented in its own blind-spot file and then trusted the tick anyway.
prompt-correctness.mjs.whyKnownPatterns: The substring IS the question here, not a shortcut around a field. This file is a test oracle: it asserts that asking for 'something dark' returns Dark-prefixed or villain-affiliated cards, and in this game villain affiliation is expressed as a NAME PREFIX — Dark Charizard, Team Rocket's Nidoking, Giovanni's Machamp. There is no villain field to match on instead, so matching the prefix is matching the structure the cards actually carry. Acknowledged rather than removed because the danger the shape names — a name match standing in for a field that exists — does not apply where the field does not exist.

prompt-audit.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the right cards are the BEST cards, and whether a prompt I did not think of works. 56 is broad but it is still my imagination.
prompt-audit.mjs.history: Found grass pokemon returning Pokemon Catcher and Pokemon Center Lady — Trainers literally named Pokemon.

env-matrix.mjs.cannotCatch: A real browser quirk none of the nine profiles model, and anything about RENDERING. It proves the script runs, never that the page looks right.
env-matrix.mjs.history: Nine profiles modelled on how browsers actually fail rather than on their names.

save-paths.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the file that lands is CORRECT. It proves each button succeeds or explains itself; it never opens the resulting image.
save-paths.mjs.history: Found open-in-a-tab silent on success — the LAST RESORT path, reached by somebody for whom the other three already failed.

user-journeys.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the session felt good. It proves nothing throws across seven sequences in four browsers; it has no view on confusion.
user-journeys.mjs.history: Sessions rather than single actions, because every real failure came from state left by the previous step.

hook-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the hook is INTERESTING, and whether the number is still true. It proves every hook loads the exact cards it names and that no price claim rests on a card without a price — it cannot tell you a 40x gap is boring, or that a price moved since the build.
hook-guard.mjs.history: Written after 138 of 230 hooks named a card the editor does not ship — I checked against card-index.json (16,468) while the editor carries 6,725 post-worthy cards, and the cheap half of a price-gap hook is exactly the $2 card that filter removes.

doc-numbers.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the PROSE is accurate. It compares four counts against the data and has no view on whether a description of how something works is still true.
doc-numbers.mjs.history: Written after I produced four handover documents from cached figures and every one was wrong on all four counts, because a rebase pulled in work between reading and writing.

read-metrics.mjs.cannotCatch: Measures raw views; cannot measure monetization-qualifying impressions. public_metrics.impression_count counts every impression from anywhere — replies, non-subscribers, the same account twice, promoted placement. A qualified impression is a unique Home Timeline impression from an X Premium subscriber with at least 50% of the post visible, and no API endpoint reports it. The gap between the two numbers is unknown and unknowable from here, so a post reading 127,200 views may be worth anywhere from zero to 127,200 against the 500,000 threshold. SECOND BLIND SPOT, added 2026-08-25 when the fetch command landed: it can only read posts the QUEUE knows about. fetch walks data/post-queue.json for rows with status "sent" and a tweetId, so anything Tyler posts by hand from his phone has no row, is never read, and never reaches data/post-outcomes.json. The outcome log therefore describes machine-sent posts only. That is a SYSTEMATIC bias, not a random one, and it points the wrong way: the posts most likely to be typed by hand are the spontaneous ones, which is exactly the class the three-engines hypothesis makes claims about.
read-metrics.mjs.coveredBy: Qualified impressions: NOTHING AUTOMATED, only a human opening Creator Studio, queued to ask-eyes for Tyler. Hand-posted coverage: nothing yet — it needs a backfill path that takes a tweet id or url and adds a sent row to the queue, which does not exist.
read-metrics.mjs.fetchVerification: Every branch of fetch is covered by an offline harness (34 checks: mapping, the 200-with-errors deleted case, missing impression_count, 500, 429, dry-run, idempotence, and the 48h promotion), and the refusal that matters most was negative-proven by disabling it — it then wrote views:null and reported NaN views as a success. The signer is proven against the live endpoint (GET /2/users/me returned 200 as @LongedEth). What is NOT proven: a fetch against a real post, because the queue has never sent one. The first live run remains a test.

originality-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether X's reviewers agree with the originality claim we stored. It checks that a claim EXISTS and is specific, not that it is correct or that anyone else would accept it. A confident, well-written, wrong claim passes every check in the file. It also cannot see the image — it reads the caption and the stored claim, so a post whose art is a straight reupload with a good sentence attached passes. It also cannot distinguish a queue that passed from a queue that was empty except by saying so in words, which it now does: nothing checked is printed as NOTHING CHECKED, not as zero failures. And it never sees the image, so a straight reupload with a well-written claim attached passes every check in the file.
originality-guard.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler's judgement, and ultimately X's. Nothing in this repo.

outcome-report.mjs.cannotCatch: WHY anything performed as it did. It reads outcomes, never causes. A post that did well because a large account replied to it, because the art was trending, or because it went out during a set reveal looks identical here to one that did well because the shape was right - and the shape is the only thing this log is set up to credit, which is exactly the direction the reader is primed to read it in. IT ALSO CANNOT SEE: qualified impressions, which are the figure the Original Content Rewards threshold is counted in and which no API reports, so nothing this report prints speaks to monetization progress; and any post not sent through the queue, because it reads data/post-outcomes.json and a post typed by hand from a phone never gets a row. That last gap is SYSTEMATIC rather than random - the posts most likely to be written by hand are the spontaneous ones, which is the class the shape hypotheses make claims about.
outcome-report.mjs.coveredBy: Causes: nothing automated, and nothing that could be. Qualified impressions: a human opening Creator Studio, queued to ask-eyes. Hand-posted coverage: nothing yet - it needs a backfill path that takes a tweet id and adds a sent row, which does not exist.
outcome-report.mjs.advisoryOnly: Registered in fleet.mjs as blocking:false on purpose. Its most common correct output is that the data cannot answer the question, and a guard that halts a build for that would be halting it for the normal state of an honest log.

search-gauntlet.mjs.cannotCatch: IT TESTS THAT RELATIONS ARE TRUE IN OUR CATALOGUE. IT NEVER TESTS THAT OUR CATALOGUE IS TRUE. Every check re-derives a claim from the same rows the claim was built from, so a wrong artist credit in card-catalogue.json passes every assertion here and ships as a confident, verified-looking sentence in a post. The data is upstream of this guard and this guard cannot see upstream. It also cannot see: whether a query returns the card a PERSON meant, only whether it returns the card the query describes; whether the relation chosen is the INTERESTING one, since it ranks nothing; and whether the editor renders any of this, because it reads the index out of build.html and never runs the page.
search-gauntlet.mjs.coveredBy: Catalogue truth: the pokemontcg.io verification ritual in card-composite.mjs, a human reading the printed credit line on the rendered card, and nothing else. That ritual is per-post and manual, and it is the only thing standing between a bad row and a public claim.
search-gauntlet.mjs.performanceNote: The mobile timing is a PROJECTION, not a measurement. Worst-case query is measured on the desk machine and multiplied by 4 for a mid-range phone. No phone has ever run it. If the multiplier is wrong the budget is wrong.

security-agent.mjs.cannotCatch: ANY SECRET WITHOUT A DISTINCTIVE SHAPE. It matches prefixes and structures - sk-ant-, gh[pousr]_, AKIA, Discord webhook URLs, PEM headers, and long tokens assigned to a variable named key/secret/token/password. A Formspree form id is eight lowercase letters and is indistinguishable from a word, so it matched nothing, and one sat in TEN tracked files while this agent ran daily through generate-pulse and reported clean. It also cannot see git history, and cannot judge whether a value SHOULD be secret - it knows shapes, not intent.
security-agent.mjs.coveredBy: scripts/secret-scan.mjs, which scans every tracked file for the actual VALUES in .env rather than guessing what a secret looks like. Blocking.
security-agent.mjs.declaredLate: This agent's own header says an agent implying total coverage is worse than none, and it had no declared blind spot at all until 2026-08-25 - after the gap it was arguing against had already cost ten files. It now prints its detects/cannot-detect list on every run.
security-agent.mjs.severityBlindSpot: IT COULD NOT TELL A LEAKED SECRET FROM A NECESSARILY-PUBLIC ENDPOINT, and called both CRITICAL. The Formspree form action must appear in the HTML a browser downloads or the waitlist does not work, so the agent was blocking on a condition that could not be satisfied without breaking the product. A blocking guard that cannot be satisfied gets ignored, and an ignored guard is worse than none: it is a red light everyone has learned to drive through, and it launders the real ones parked beside it. Fixed 2026-08-25 by splitting SEVERITY from VISIBILITY - such values are now INVENTORY, named every run with what an attacker can and cannot do, and never a failure. The agent still cannot judge INTENT: it is TOLD which endpoints are intentional; it cannot work that out for itself.

secret-scan.mjs.cannotCatch: A SECRET THAT IS NOT IN .env. It checks the values we hold against every tracked file, so a credential that was never written to .env is invisible to it. It also cannot check git history - a value already committed stays readable forever and no scan of the working tree will say so. Values shorter than six characters are skipped as too noisy to search for.
secret-scan.mjs.cannotFix: A CLIENT-SIDE FORM ENDPOINT IS PUBLIC BY DESIGN. It sits in the HTML a browser downloads, so it is readable the moment the form works. This guard reports generated artifacts that carry one on every run, and blocks only on SOURCE files. Secrecy is not the control there - Formspree's domain restriction and spam filtering are.
secret-scan.mjs.theReasoning: REVOKING COMES FIRST, BECAUSE REMOVAL DOES NOT UN-SHARE WHAT WAS ALREADY SHARED. This is the whole doctrine of the guard and it lived only inside an error string, one refactor away from being lost. Deleting a credential from a file changes what happens NEXT; it does nothing about every copy already fetched, cached, forked or read. So the order is always: revoke or rotate at the provider first, then clean the files. A cleanup that feels like a fix and leaves a live credential in the world is worse than no cleanup, because it ends the sense of urgency without ending the exposure.
secret-scan.mjs.andItsLimit: That doctrine has one exception this guard must state or it will mislead: a value that is public BY DESIGN cannot be revoked into privacy. A client-side form endpoint is in the HTML a browser downloads. Rotating it replaces one public string with another public string - worth doing if the current one is being abused, pointless as a secrecy measure. For those, the control is the provider's own domain restriction and spam filtering, never obscurity.

artifact-drift.mjs.cannotCatch: WHICH OF THE TWO IS CORRECT. It can only say that the committed page and a fresh build disagree - never which one is right. The committed page may be stale, or the generator may have just been changed and the rebuild IS the correct new output. A human has to look. It also cannot check an artifact whose generator will not run: generate-pulse.mjs currently fails, so the-pulse.html and print-watch.html are UNCHECKED and reported as such rather than silently passing.
artifact-drift.mjs.alsoCannot: See drift in anything that is not generated HTML under research/assets - JSON feeds, the app bundle and the newsletter are outside it. And it strips timestamps and dates before comparing, so a page whose ONLY change is a date it stamps itself reads as matching. That is deliberate: without it every page is permanently stale and the check becomes noise nobody reads.
artifact-drift.mjs.whyAdvisory: Blocking would stop a build because a price refreshed an hour ago. The failure this guards against is nobody LOOKING - promo.html was published saying 'Goodnight.' over a Musharna while its generator had moved to 'Waitlist open.' Naming it is enough.

visual-claim-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: A false visual claim phrased about ONE card. It only fires when a drawn feature is asserted across a whole population — 'every card', 'all of them'. 'There is a Pikachu on this card' is equally unverifiable from our data and passes silently, because we hold no field describing artwork at all. It also matches on wording, so a claim built from a synonym it does not know is invisible to it.
visual-claim-guard.mjs.coveredBy: Tyler's eyes, and the house rule that artwork claims belong to whoever can see the art

reveal-watch-guard.mjs.cannotCatch: A human copying a reveal out of the queue and posting it by hand. It proves reveal-watch.mjs has no CODE PATH to the send gate; it cannot prevent a person from reading the file and pasting. It also only inspects the files it is told to watch, so a new script that reaches the send path is invisible until somebody adds it to WATCHED.
reveal-watch-guard.mjs.coveredBy: send-gate's own confirm step, which is a separate control on the human path

response-audit.mjs.cannotCatch: Whether the check it found is CORRECT. It sees that res.ok or stop_reason is read somewhere in the window; it cannot tell a real guard from `if (res.ok) {}`. It also knows only the completeness signals listed in HOST_RULES, so a new provider with a new field passes until somebody teaches it. And a declared RESPONSE-AUDIT-OK waiver is taken at its word — the reason is never validated.
response-audit.mjs.coveredBy: code review, and the fact that a wrong waiver has to be written deliberately
